record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: If Q is a nondegenerate positive definite quadratic form of dimension d≥3 that is not a multiple of a rational form, do the gaps between consecutive elements of {Q(x):x∈Z^d} go to zero as Q(x)→∞?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 44 (Davenport-Lewis). Suppose that Q is not a multiple of a ratio-nal form. Then the gaps between consecutive elements of the s et {Q(x) : x ∈ Zd } go to zero as Q (x) → ∞ .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ and let $Q : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a nondegenerate positive definite quadratic form, i.e., $Q(x) = x^T A x$ for some symmetric positive definite $d \times d$ real matrix $A$. Assume that $Q$ is not a scalar multiple of any quadratic form with rational coefficients. Consider the set of values
$$V(Q) = \{ Q(x) : x \in \mathbb{Z}^d \} \subset [0,\infty),$$
and enumerate its elements in increasing order as $0 = v_0 < v_1 < v_2 < \cdots$. Prove or disprove: the consecutive gaps tend to zero, i.e.,
$$v_{n+1} - v_n \to 0 \quad \text{as } n \to \infty.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been established for dimensions $d \geq 9$ by Bentkus and Götze, and subsequently extended to $d \geq 5$ by Götze using lattice point estimates for irrational ellipsoids. The cases $d = 3$ and $d = 4$ remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lattice point problems and values of quadratic forms (Götze)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the Davenport-Lewis conjecture on gaps between values of positive definite irrational quadratic forms in dimension d ≥ 5.
status_evidence.claim: The Davenport-Lewis gap conjecture is proved for d ≥ 5.

status_evidence.title: Lattice point problems and distribution of values of quadratic forms (Bentkus-Götze)
status_evidence.snippet: For d ≥ 9, proves the Davenport-Lewis conjecture that gaps between successive values of irrational positive definite quadratic forms tend to zero.
status_evidence.claim: Bentkus and Götze proved the conjecture for d ≥ 9.
